title: Handoff tether: customer network onboarding - PRD brain dump
content:
Context / intent:
This is a messy brain-dump of ideas for a lightweight 'tethered handoff' onboarding flow for customer-managed networks (VPCs / on-prem edge). Goal: let customers opt into a short-lived, observable tether that: 1) proves connectivity and telemetry for onboarding, 2) captures deterministic audit evidence for approval gates, and 3) can be torn down automatically after a configurable grace window.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers onboarding private deployments often want a minimal, low-trust way to prove their network topology and connectivity without handing over long-lived credentials.
- Current onboarding flows either: require manual screenshots and emails (slow, un-auditable) or permanent agents (high friction, security concerns).
- We need consistent audit records for approvals and for SOC/infosec review; the format should be compact and queryable.

Core goals:
- Short-lived tether: ephemeral connection agent that runs in customer environment for a limited time (default 72h) and emits an immutable audit bundle.
- Approval gates: allow product to require operator consent before production traffic is allowed; gates should be attachable to onboarding steps and enforceable by the control plane.
- Compact evidence: produce a compact, signed artifact (zip/ndjson) that contains connection traces, certificate fingerprints, operator attestation token, and diffed network snapshot.
- Low privilege: tether runs with minimal privileges (eg. only outbound TLS to control plane, no inbound firewall openings).
- UX: minimal customer clicks — operator clicks "approve" in console, optionally provide short justification.

Proposed tether flow (high level):
1) Customer starts onboarding in Console -> chooses "Tethered proof".
2) Console emits a short-lived onboarding token (15 min) and a small bootstrap package (single binary or container) with instructions.
3) Customer runs binary in their environment: it opens an outbound TLS connection to Redwood control plane, collects local network metadata (interfaces, routing table, k8s node list if present), performs a small echo test to target endpoints, and fetches configured ingress CIDR(s).
4) The tether computes a digest of artifacts, signs it with ephemeral keypair, streams the bundle to control plane.
5) Control plane persists immutable audit bundle (content-addressable), indexes it, and surfaces an approval card in Console.
6) Operator(s) review the card, optionally request replay or additional probes, then click APPROVE / REJECT. Approve creates a signed approval record linked to the bundle.
7) If approved and policy allows, onboarding transitions to next step (e.g., creating route/peering). If not approved within grace window, tether is revoked and any temporary routes are cleaned.

Example audit bundle contents (flat list to keep small):
- bundle_id: sha256 digest (string)
- bundle_version: "v1"
- timestamp: ISO8601
- ephemeral_pubkey: base64
- signed_manifest: base64(sig over manifest)
- manifest: ndjson lines (human readable) listing: host:ip, interface, cidr, route-table-show, k8s-nodes-count, local-ps-output-short, probe-results
- probe_samples: short list of tcp/https handshake latencies and cert fingerprints
- operator_snapshot: base64-encoded operator-supplied note (optional)
- retention_hint: policy tag (72h_proof, 1yr_evidence, etc.)

Approval gate modes (configurable per-customer / per-flow):
- manual (default): human review required, one or more approvers defined in customer account.
- delegated: customer designates an operator role that can auto-approve for low-risk changes (uses RBAC mapping).
- auto-approve-on-pass: tether runs a set of probes and heuristics; if all heuristics pass (no open ports, expected CIDR, trusted cert fingerprints), the system auto-approves and records audit.
- grace-period: allow a configurable timeout where approvals are implicit if not explicitly rejected (for low-friction onboarding).

Audit log indexing & query surface (Console & API):
- index keys: bundle_id, customer_id, operator_id, ip_ranges, route-ids, created_at, approved_at, approval_mode, attest_token_id
- user queries we should support: "show bundles for customer X in last 7 days", "show approvals that approved without manual eyes", "diff bundle A -> bundle B"
- export formats: ndjson, minimal JSON summary, signed-zip for legal/compliance export.

Security/forensics considerations:
- All artifacts must be content-addressed and tamper-evident (signature chain).
- Ephemeral key lifecycle: tether holds ephemeral key; control plane issues onboarding token tied to ephemeral key fingerprint.
- Minimal data collection: redact sensitive fields by default (e.g., hostnames, usernames) unless customer opts in to full capture.
- Key rotation & escrow: provide customer option to escrow a public key for long-term evidence verification.

Operator UX (console notes):
- Approval card shows: summary (CIDRs, routes, k8s node count), small probe health map, risk score (heuristic), quick links: "view full bundle", "request replay", "mark follow-up ticket".
- Make it keyboard-friendly: approve keyboard shortcut, one-click escalate to SOC.
- Email/Slack notification options for approvers.

Retention & cost model (rough):
- Proof bundles: default 90 days retained as compressed bundles.
- Compliance bundles: customer can opt into 1-7 year retention (billable addon).
- We store a compact index for all bundles indefinitely for metadata queries; actual bundle binary may be archived to cheaper storage.

Edge-case scenarios and resiliency:
- If tether cannot reach control plane, it caches manifests and retries; provide offline proof mode where agent packages and provides signed bundle to customer for upload.
- Partial probe failures: mark bundle as PARTIAL and allow operator to request rerun before approval.
- Stale approvals: approval records must include the exact bundle digest; if config changes after approval, subsequent actions must verify they match the approved bundle.

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- How much local probing is acceptable before it violates customer security policy? (ask SE during pilot)
- Should we require out-of-band validation (phone call) for high-risk customers?
- What exactly should the default retention be to balance cost vs compliance requests?
- Do we allow the tether to modify anything (eg. create temporary peering) or strictly read-only?

Pilot plan (MVP):
- Build minimal agent (go binary) that collects metadata, signs manifest, and uploads to control plane (no automatic changes).
- Console: approval card + manual approve button + export bundle.
- Short pilot with 2 customers + 1 partner SE team. Collect feedback on heuristics and what information they need to approve.

Next immediate todos (for this doc):
- [ ] Get alignment with SE and SRE on allowed probes and default timeout values. (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Draft minimal API contract for bundle ingest and indexing. (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Prototype small approval-card UI in Figma and run internal review. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Create a small evaluation checklist for pilot customers.

Notes to self:
- Keep artifacts tiny (ndjson preferred) to avoid egress cost to customer.
- Consider an option to provide bundles as signed OCI blobs for reproducible storage.

References / links: 
- Confluence note: PD-781 (tethered onboarding overview)
- Jira PRD ticket: PRD-1447
- Related prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/handshake-agent (dev branch)

If we like this direction, follow up with a thinner PRD that expands the audit schema and enumerates heuristics for the auto-approve mode.
